title: ISUZU UNIVERSE | Internal Action Centre (local sources)

source_policy: Metrics are calculated directly from local workstation source files under 01_data. Where a primary source could not fully verify a paper-reported figure (AC-05), both figures are shown with the gap stated, not resolved. No owner, due date, dealer fleet, causal price effect, tender value or intervention result is invented.

cases.title: Brake pads

headline.label: Change in parts billed
headline.basis: ISZE to Isuzu Truck UK; brake-pad subgroup

cases.summary: Unit purchasing fell faster than billed value. Start with a distributor review, not a claim about dealer losses.
cases.context_line: 44 dealers in the IDS UK CV (trucks) network, 20 Sept 2026 | not a sales-to-dealer denominator

chart.title: Parts billed to Isuzu Truck UK
chart.caption: Full calendar years; brake-pad subgroup. Not sales to end customers.

facts: The IDS Dealer Standards network lists 44 dealers under UK CV (trucks) as of 20 September 2026. This is a ranking-programme listing, not a sales-to-dealer purchasing count.
Relevant fleet by dealer and validated brake-pad applicability are not supplied. No dealer service-demand rate is calculated.
cases.interpretation: The subgroup has a measured purchasing decline. A lower share of brake pads in a dealer's own 2025 parts purchases would be a mix signal, not proof of lost maintenance business.
cases.limitation: No dealer-year comparison, causal price effect or dealer performance ranking is established here. No sales-to-dealer file was located locally to cross-check dealer-level demand.
cases.next_action: Review the distributor decline with ITUK. Then compare dealer-level brake-pad share once a sales-to-dealer extract is available.
checks: Confirm the brake-pad subgroup membership before any product-specific intervention.
Keep dealer network listings separate from distributor purchasing change.
Treat mix differences as questions, not service-demand gaps.

references.method: Change = 2025 total_eur_2025 minus total_eur_2024. Percentage change = (2025/2024 - 1) x 100.
Count of rows with ids_tab = 'UK CV'.

cases.title: Oil filters

headline.label: Of modelled service need supplied
headline.basis: Measured units divided by modelled expected units

cases.summary: Check the fleet denominator before using this as a distributor performance example.
cases.context_line: 10,746 EUR parts billed | 13,780 modelled vehicles (service model)
cases.basis_label: Modelled expectation + measured purchasing | local source file

metrics.label: Modelled value difference
metrics.basis: Source-reported service gap; not recoverable sales

chart.title: Purchasing against modelled oil-filter need
chart.caption: Calendar 2025. The unfilled share is a model difference, not proven competitor sales.

facts: Measured oil-filter units: 2,029; modelled expected units: 13,494.5.
The service-model fleet and expected units are used exactly as supplied. The spend-model fleet is shown separately, not blended.
The two fleet bases disagree by 925 vehicles for the same market and year; the reason is not established here.
cases.interpretation: Purchasing is below the selected model expectation. Fleet-basis disagreement needs checking before assigning a commercial cause.
cases.limitation: No German dealer attribution, end-customer demand or alternate supplier is measured. The modelled value difference is not an expected sales gain.
cases.next_action: Reconcile why the service-model and spend-model fleet counts differ, then request sales-to-dealer information for the same scope.
checks: Document why the two fleet bases differ before quoting either as definitive.
Request dealer-level purchases only after agreeing the comparison scope.
Out-of-range service percentages stay withheld, not capped.

references.method: Displayed percentage = actual_qty / expected_qty x 100. Rates outside 0-100 are withheld, never capped.
Fleet basis comparison only; not used in the service-demand coverage figure.

cases.title: Air filters
cases.summary: BVP enters the scope in 2025. Separate the mix change from any pricing conclusion.
cases.context_line: 47,783 vehicles in the 2025 fleet-basis file | not a dealer fleet denominator
cases.basis_label: Measured purchasing mix | local source file

metrics.label: BVP entry, 2025
metrics.basis: BVP = Best Value Parts; zero in this 2024 scope

chart.title: Genuine and BVP, IUK air filters
chart.caption: ISZE to IUK; full calendar years. BVP = Best Value Parts.

facts: Genuine parts billed rise within the scope; BVP adds a separate new contribution. BVP accounts for 53.1% of the increase in billed value.
Market fleet context: 47,783 vehicles in the 2025 fleet-basis file. This is not a dealer fleet denominator.
cases.interpretation: No immediate price action is indicated by this purchasing evidence alone. The BVP entry is part of the observed growth, not evidence of a price-response relationship.
cases.limitation: Distributor-level concession share for this scope is reported separately in AC-04's family view, not blended here. No competitor retail price is compared with a dealer reference price.
cases.next_action: Review the Genuine/BVP change on this scope. Cross-check against the family-level concession share before any price recommendation.
checks: Keep Genuine and BVP visible on the same scope.
Do not blend the product-mix and concession totals.
Any later competitor comparison needs matched tax, channel, pack and applicability.

references.method: Total = genuine_eur + bvp_eur. BVP contribution to growth = change in BVP euro / change in total euro.

cases.title: Don't Lose the Deal

headline.label: Credits found in a targeted billing search
headline.basis: 3 credit memos tagged DLOD/dlod, local billing extracts; paper reports 90,000 EUR

cases.summary: A targeted search of local billing extracts finds 65,304.37 EUR in DLOD-tagged credits, 24,695.63 EUR short of the paper's 90,000 EUR. Neither figure is a full case register.
cases.basis_label: Partially verified against primary billing | case register still missing

metrics.label: Found in billing search (3 credit memos)
metrics.basis: Search of order-header and billing extracts for PO/reference containing DLOD

chart.title: Don't Lose the Deal credits: billing search vs paper
chart.caption: Billing search covers cy2023_2024.csv, cy2026_q1.csv and order_headers_from_Order_Detail.csv in 01_data/00_derived. No case register was found for any of the three credits.

facts: 2024-01-03: 5,304.37 EUR — REBATE, PO ref 'DLOD 2023 Q3+Q4'; Sold-to 2194 Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd (source: cy2023_2024.csv).
2025-02-14: 30,000.00 EUR — CR, PO ref 'DLOD'; Sold-to 2194 Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd (source: order_headers_from_Order_Detail.csv / cy2025 (order header)).
2026-03-30: 30,000.00 EUR — CR REBATE, PO ref 'dlod'; Sold-to 2575 Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd (source: order_headers_from_Order_Detail.csv + cy2026_q1.csv).
The billing search covers three files (cy2023_2024.csv, cy2026_q1.csv, order_headers_from_Order_Detail.csv) in 01_data/00_derived; it is not a certified complete search of every billing year.
The gap to the paper's 90,000 EUR (24,695.63 EUR) is unresolved: it may be earlier 2023 credits not tagged 'DLOD' in these files, a different labelling, or a scope difference.
cases.interpretation: The billing search corroborates part of the paper's total with primary evidence, but does not reconcile it. No supported case, dealer, part or outcome record was found for any of the three credits.
cases.limitation: This is a targeted text search on a purchase-order/reference field, not a full programme credit ledger or case register. The 2023 Q3+Q4 credit is a single combined line; it cannot be split into the paper's implied quarterly cadence.
cases.next_action: Ask Isuzu Truck UK to reconcile the gap, confirm whether earlier 2023 credits carry a different label, and supply the case register (part, dealer, competitor evidence, support granted, outcome) for all credits.
checks: Do not treat the billing-search total as the full programme total.
Reconcile all credits to a ledger before treating either total as verified.
Collect part, dealer, dated competitor evidence, support granted and outcome for each credit.

references.method: Text search for DLOD/dlod in the purchase-order-number / PO-reference column; matched rows aggregated by date and amount.
Extract the reported amount from the document text.

cases.title: Tender deadlines and outcomes

headline.label: Distinct opportunities in the current local feed

cases.summary: Computed directly from the local tender feed. The feed is dated; confirm it has been refreshed before assigning opportunities today.

metrics.label: Due within 14 days (as of the feed's own generation date)

chart.title: Tender funnel, local feed
chart.caption: tender_data.json, generated 2026-09-22T17:24:26.467020Z. Not re-derived against today's date.

facts: Local file tender_data.json was generated 2026-09-22T17:24:26.467020Z; this build ran on 2026-09-24, so the feed is a few days old, not a live query.
'Due within 14 days' is the count as computed inside the feed at its own generation time; it has not been recalculated against today's review date in this build.
0 outcomes are recorded in the feed; win rate is reported as 'insufficient data' (minimum sample for a rate: 20).
cases.interpretation: The local feed is available and matches the white paper's page-22 snapshot exactly, confirming both draw from the same underlying refresh. Refresh again before allocating today's effort if more than a few days have passed.
cases.limitation: No fleet make, truck count, tender value or maintenance-part demand is inferred beyond what the feed stores. The 14-day countdown is not recomputed against the current date in this build.
cases.next_action: Re-run the tender feed refresh if it is more than a few days old, recompute deadlines against today's date, assign relevant opportunities, and record won, lost or declined outcomes as they close.
checks: Confirm the feed's generation date before quoting a deadline count as current.
Check aftersales relevance without assuming Isuzu fleet make.
Record owner, pursuit decision and closure outcome separately.

references.method: Read directly from tender_data.json, generated 2026-09-22T17:24:26.467020Z. No values recomputed or refreshed.
